newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-SHARP OUT OF INDY 500, FOYT PURSUES ANDRETTI.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SHARP OUT OF INDY 500, FOYT PURSUES ANDRETTI.

text.p: Scott Sharp was declared out of the Indy 500 Monday due to injuries suffered in a crash Friday, and team owner A.J. Foyt renewed his pursuit of NASCAR driver John Andretti to steer one of the Foyt team's three entries.

"We elected not to have Scott drive," Foyt said. "We are going to stick with the doctors; they know best. We definitely do not want anything to happen to Scott, and we do not want to take any chances."
Foyt said Sharp, co-champion of the first Indy Racing League season, suffered a brain contusion and needs time to mend.
"We are working with my godson, John Andretti. I spoke with Cale Yarborough (Andretti's NASCAR team owner), and we are good friends," said four-time Indy winner Foyt.
"I've asked him for a big favour. John's a great race driver, and he's driven for me before. It's going to be hard to get him back and forth, but whatever we can work out. His schedule is tight."

Andretti, the only driver to race in both the Indy 500 and the NASCAR Coca-Cola 600 on the same day, appeared to be out of consideration for the Indy 500 when rain forced NASCAR to reschedule the Winston 500 for last Saturday. Andretti qualified on the pole for that race, and without having a shot at a top starting spot he said he wasn't going to run at Indy.
But with Foyt in a pinch, Andretti's position began softening and he said he would further talk with Foyt following Saturday's race.
Denise Wood, Andretti spokesperson, confirmed that Andretti has talked with Foyt, and said Andretti told Foyt he would make a decision Tuesday.
The NASCAR series Coca-Cola 600 starts a couple of hours after the conclusion of the Indy 500.

Foyt projected that Andretti, a former Indy car driver with a win in the CART series race in Australia to his credit, would likely practice at the Brickyard Wednesday or Thursday and would qualify for the race Sunday -- the final day of qualifying.
"John's a race driver, and it won't take him long to adapt to anything," Foyt said.
